bundle_vector_borne/dist/vector_borne.pa.short_description: FIPS code identifier for the row: '00' for national rows, 2-digit state/territory FIPS for state rows, and 5-digit county FIPS for county rows.
bundle_vector_borne/dist/vector_borne.pa.long_description: FIPS code identifying the geography of the row: '00' for national rows, a 2-digit state/territory FIPS code for state rows, and a 5-digit county FIPS code for county rows. Connecticut reported by county through 2022 and by planning region (FIPS 09110-09190) from 2023 onward, so its county FIPS codes change mid-series.

bundle_vector_borne/dist/vector_borne.pa.short_description: 1 if the Epic Cosmos value was suppressed (10 or fewer patients) and imputed, 0 otherwise; NA for other sources.
bundle_vector_borne/dist/vector_borne.pa.long_description: Epic Cosmos suppresses counts of 10 or fewer. Those cells are imputed as 5 and flagged 1. A disease's count and percent measures share one flag, and the denominators (patients with a new vector-borne diagnosis, all lab component results) have their own. ArboNET and NNDSS rows are NA.

arbonet_eee_cases.long_name: Eastern equine encephalitis virus human disease cases reported to ArboNET
arbonet_eee_cases.short_description: Human Eastern equine encephalitis virus disease cases reported to CDC's ArboNET surveillance system.
arbonet_eee_cases.long_description: Total reported human disease cases of Eastern equine encephalitis (EEE) virus, including both neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive presentations, as reported to CDC's ArboNET national arboviral surveillance system by state and local health departments. Coverage begins in 2003.

arbonet_eee_neuro_cases.long_name: Eastern equine encephalitis virus human neuroinvasive disease cases reported to ArboNET
arbonet_eee_neuro_cases.short_description: Human Eastern equine encephalitis virus neuroinvasive disease cases reported to CDC's ArboNET surveillance system.
arbonet_eee_neuro_cases.long_description: Reported human cases of Eastern equine encephalitis (EEE) virus neuroinvasive disease (meningitis, encephalitis, or acute flaccid paralysis), as reported to CDC's ArboNET national arboviral surveillance system. This is a subset of arbonet_eee_cases. Because severe neuroinvasive illness is far more likely to be diagnosed and reported than milder non-neuroinvasive illness, CDC considers neuroinvasive counts the more reliable basis for comparing disease activity across locations and over time. Coverage begins in 2003.

arbonet_eee_nonhuman_activity.long_description: Binary indicator that equals 1 when veterinary disease cases, or infections in mosquitoes, birds, or sentinel animals, were reported to CDC's ArboNET system for the geography and year, and 0 when no such activity was reported.

arbonet_wnv_blood_donors.long_description: Count of presumptive viremic blood donors, defined by CDC as people who had no symptoms at the time of donating blood but whose blood tested positive when screened for West Nile virus. Identified through blood supply screening rather than clinical care, so counted separately from reported human disease cases. Reported for West Nile virus only, as it is the only one of ArboNET's arboviruses with routine blood donor screening.

bundle_vector_borne/dist/vector_borne.pa.short_description: Value for the vector-borne disease measure identified by the measure column: annual case/activity counts as reported to ArboNET (national, state, and county), weekly case counts for the NNDSS measures (national and state only), or monthly Epic Cosmos new-diagnosis and lab-test counts and percents (national and state only). NNDSS publishes cumulative year-to-date counts; this bundle de-cumulates them into weekly incident counts by differencing consecutive weeks within each MMWR year, so occasional negative values reflect downward revisions to the source's cumulative totals.

arbonet.name: ArboNET Arboviral Disease Surveillance System
arbonet.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Division of Vector-Borne Diseases
arbonet.description: ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system managed by CDC together with state and territorial health departments. In addition to human disease, ArboNET maintains data on arboviral infections among presumptive viremic blood donors, veterinary disease cases, mosquitoes, dead birds, and sentinel animals. Human cases are reported by county of residence rather than location of exposure, and are assigned to the year of illness onset. Several caveats apply: under-reporting is inherent to any surveillance system that depends on clinicians suspecting the disease, ordering the appropriate test, and reporting confirmed results; non-neuroinvasive cases are substantially more under-reported than neuroinvasive cases, so total case counts should not be used to compare disease activity between locations or over time; and there is a lag in reporting to CDC. Connecticut reported by county through 2022 and by planning region from 2023 onward, so its geography codes change mid-series. Reporting years differ by disease and the most recent year is preliminary and subject to change.
arbonet.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

nnds.name: National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System (NNDSS)
nnds.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
nnds.description: The National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System (NNDSS) is a nationwide collaboration that enables all levels of public health to share notifiable disease related health information. Public health uses this information to monitor, control, and prevent the occurrence and spread of state-reportable and nationally notifiable infectious and some non-infectious diseases and conditions. NNDSS publishes weekly cumulative year-to-date case counts; this bundle de-cumulates them (by differencing consecutive weeks within each MMWR year) into weekly incident counts covering vector-borne, tick-borne, and travel-associated arboviral and parasitic diseases: the eight ArboNET-overlapping arboviral diseases NNDSS also tracks by weekly provisional count (chikungunya, Eastern/Western equine encephalitis, Jamestown Canyon, La Crosse, Powassan, St. Louis encephalitis, and West Nile virus disease), babesiosis, dengue and dengue-like illness, ehrlichiosis/anaplasmosis, malaria, and non-congenital Zika virus disease. Negative values in case counts reflect retroactive corrections by the CDC.
nnds.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

epic_vector_borne.name: Epic Cosmos
epic_vector_borne.description: Epic Cosmos is a collaborative research platform containing de-identified patient data from hospitals and health systems using Epic electronic health record systems, accessed via SlicerDicer. This bundle includes monthly counts of new diagnoses (first diagnosis of the disease with none in the prior 6 months) and of lab component results for Lyme disease, babesiosis, malaria, Rocky Mountain spotted fever, West Nile virus and dengue, by state of residence. Percent measures are shares of patients with a new vector-borne diagnosis (new cases) or of all lab component results (tests), not positivity rates. Counts of 10 or fewer are suppressed and imputed as 5. Malaria and dengue in the US are mostly travel-associated.
epic_vector_borne.restrictions: The data can be re-used with appropriate attribution. A suggested citation relating to this data is 'Results of research performed with Epic Cosmos were obtained from the PopHIVE platform (https://github.com/PopHIVE/Ingest).'
